Dialog.UsageGuide.Title: Usage Guide
Guide.Article.welcome.Title: Welcome
Guide.Article.welcome.Summary: Learn what the level editor can do and where to begin.
Guide.Article.welcome.Intro: Cut the Rope DX: Level Editor creates and edits levels for Cut the Rope: DX. Use the palette to add objects, the canvas to arrange them, and the inspector to organize layers and edit exact values.
Guide.Article.welcome.Route.Heading: A good first route
Guide.Article.welcome.Route.Steps:
Create a level and choose its size and background.
Drag Om Nom, candy, a rope hook, and stars from the palette.
Arrange the objects on the canvas, then save the level.
Use File > Playtest to try it in Cut the Rope: DX.
Guide.Article.welcome.Layout.Caption: The editor with the palette, canvas, layers, and properties labelled.
Guide.Article.welcome.Search.Tip: You can open this guide while editing and use search to jump directly to an object or shortcut.
Guide.Article.first-level.Title: Create your first level
Guide.Article.first-level.Summary: Build a small playable level from an empty document.
Guide.Article.first-level.Build.Steps:
Choose File > New and select a resolution.
Drag Om Nom and a candy from the palette onto the canvas.
Add a rope hook above the candy and bind it to the correct candy in Properties.
Add one or more stars between the candy and Om Nom.
Choose File > Save As, then File > Playtest when available.
Guide.Article.first-level.Validation.Not: The validator warns when essential objects or bindings are missing. You may still save, edit, or playtest after reviewing the warning.
Guide.Article.first-level.Example.Captio: A simple level with Om Nom, candy, a rope, and three stars.
Guide.Article.know-the-editor.Title: Know the editor
Guide.Article.know-the-editor.Summary: Identify the palette, canvas, layers, properties, and compact controls.
Guide.Article.know-the-editor.Expanded: The palette is on the left, the level canvas is in the center, and Layers and Properties share the inspector on the right. File, Edit, View, and Help commands appear in the menu bar.
Guide.Article.know-the-editor.Compact: On a narrow window, the canvas takes priority. Palette and Layers move behind bottom tabs, contextual editing actions appear near the selection, and the hamburger drawer contains the remaining commands.
Guide.Article.know-the-editor.Layouts.Ca: Expanded and compact editor layouts side by side.
Guide.Article.add-place-objects.Title: Add and place objects
Guide.Article.add-place-objects.Summary: Find objects in the palette and place them on the canvas.
Guide.Article.add-place-objects.Place.St:
Use the palette search box or expand a game group.
Drag an available object from the palette onto the level.
Drag the placed object to reposition it. Grid snapping applies when enabled.
Use Properties when an exact coordinate or object-specific value is required.
Guide.Article.add-place-objects.Availabi: Objects unavailable to the current level configuration are disabled in the palette. For example, split-candy objects require the half-candy mechanic.
Guide.Article.add-place-objects.Drag.Cap: Dragging an object from the palette to the canvas.
Guide.Article.select-transform.Title: Select and transform objects
Guide.Article.select-transform.Summary: Select one or many objects, move them, rotate them, and use contextual handles.
Guide.Article.select-transform.Selection: Click an object to select it. Command-click on macOS or Ctrl-click elsewhere adds or removes an object from the selection. Drag any selected member to move the group together.
Guide.Article.select-transform.Handles: Selected objects expose only the handles they support: rotation dials, radius rings, resize grips, rails, path points, or mechanical-hand joints.
Guide.Article.select-transform.Duplicate: Command/Ctrl-drag an already selected object past the drag threshold to duplicate the selection and move the copy.
Guide.Article.select-transform.RotationS: Hold Alt while using a rotation dial to snap temporarily. The Edit > Snap rotation toggle keeps the same behavior latched.
Guide.Article.select-transform.Handles.C: Common selection, rotation, resize, and radius handles.
Guide.Article.clipboard-lock-hide.Title: Copy, paste, lock, hide, and delete
Guide.Article.clipboard-lock-hide.Summar: Reuse objects and protect parts of a level from accidental edits.
Guide.Article.clipboard-lock-hide.Clipbo: Use Edit > Cut, Copy, Paste, Select All, and Delete, or their keyboard shortcuts. Select All targets the active layer.
Guide.Article.clipboard-lock-hide.Lockin: The Layers tree provides visibility and lock buttons for each layer and object. Double-click an object on the canvas to lock or unlock it.
Guide.Article.clipboard-lock-hide.Delete: Deleting a layer also removes every object inside it. The confirmation explains the scope, and the operation can be undone.
Guide.Article.layers.Title: Work with layers
Guide.Article.layers.Summary: Organize object drawing order and lock or hide groups of objects.
Guide.Article.layers.Intro: Layers control organization and drawing order. Use the controls beneath the tree to add, delete, move, or merge layers.
Guide.Article.layers.Organize.Steps:
Select a layer to make it active.
Rename it from the row action when a descriptive name is useful.
Drag rows to reorder layers or objects.
Use the eye and lock buttons to hide or protect a whole layer or one object.
Guide.Article.layers.InheritedState.Note: Locked or hidden parent layers affect their objects even when an individual object row appears enabled.
Guide.Article.layers.Panel.Caption: The Layers panel and its row actions.
Guide.Article.edit-properties.Title: Edit properties
Guide.Article.edit-properties.Summary: Adjust exact coordinates and object-specific behavior in the inspector.
Guide.Article.edit-properties.Fields: Select an object to show its fields in Properties. Common fields include position, rotation, size, bindings, movement, and object-specific gameplay values.
Guide.Article.edit-properties.Help: Non-obvious fields include an inline help button. Numeric fields enforce known ranges, while unknown XML attributes remain preserved when the level is saved.
Canvas handles and property fields edit the same data. Use the canvas for visual placement and Properties for exact values.
Guide.Article.level-settings.Title: Configure level settings
Guide.Article.level-settings.Summary: Choose level dimensions, mechanics, water, and visual customization.
Guide.Article.level-settings.Mechanics: Edit > Level Settings controls resolution, rope physics speed, tutorial staging, half-candy and night-level mechanics, and the mobile physics model.
Guide.Article.level-settings.Customizati: The same dialog configures water height and drain speed, rope color, background, candy skin, and Om Nom's platform. Customization choices can optionally become defaults for new levels.
Guide.Article.level-settings.Palette.Not: Changing a mechanic can alter which palette objects are valid. Review disabled objects and validation messages after changing half-candy or night-level settings.
Guide.Article.level-settings.Dialog.Capt: Level Settings with mechanics and customization sections.
Guide.Article.rope-hooks.Title: Rope hooks and candy binding
Guide.Article.rope-hooks.Summary: Connect rope hooks to the intended candy and edit movable rails and catch radii.
Guide.Article.rope-hooks.Binding: A rope hook must refer to the candy it controls. Set the candy binding in Properties, especially in split-candy levels where each half has its own number.
Guide.Article.rope-hooks.Handles: Some hooks expose a radius ring or a movement rail. Drag the ring to change its catch radius; drag a rail end to resize it, the hook to slide along it, or the bar to move the whole assembly.
Guide.Article.rope-hooks.Validation.Warn: Validation reports hooks bound to missing candies or bulbs before save or playtest.
Guide.Article.rope-hooks.Handles.Caption: A selected rope hook with radius and movable-rail handles.
Guide.Article.magic-hats.Title: Magic hats
Guide.Article.magic-hats.Summary: Pair hat entrances and exits and align their mouths.
Guide.Article.magic-hats.Pairing: Magic hats work as paired entrances and exits. Give matching hats the same pair identifier, then rotate and position their mouths for the intended launch direction.
Guide.Article.magic-hats.Mouth: Hat artwork can overlap while the interactive mouth remains elsewhere, so use hitboxes when precise portal placement matters.
Guide.Article.magic-hats.Pair.Caption: A paired set of magic hats with mouth hitboxes visible.
Guide.Article.movement-paths.Title: Movement paths
Guide.Article.movement-paths.Summary: Create orbit or polyline motion and reshape paths directly on the canvas.
Guide.Article.movement-paths.Modes: Objects that support movement can use orbit or polyline modes. Properties controls speed, direction, retracing, and whether a polyline closes into a loop.
Guide.Article.movement-paths.Edit.Steps:
Select a moving object and choose its movement mode in Properties.
For a polyline, drag the end nub or click a segment to add a point.
Drag a point to reshape the path.
Right-click any point after the starting anchor to remove it.
Guide.Article.movement-paths.Angles.Tip: Hold Shift while adding or dragging a polyline point to constrain the new segment to a snapped angle.
Guide.Article.movement-paths.Limit.Note: Polyline paths support up to 99 points. View > Show movement paths reveals paths even when their objects are not selected.
Guide.Article.movement-paths.Polyline.Ca: Editing a polyline path and its points.
Guide.Article.conveyors.Title: Conveyors and ant conveyors
Guide.Article.conveyors.Summary: Resize, rotate, and configure moving surfaces and ant paths.
Guide.Article.conveyors.Belt: Select a conveyor to reveal independent length and width handles. Use its rotation dial for orientation and Properties for movement direction and speed.
Guide.Article.conveyors.Ants: Ant conveyors follow editable paths. Shape their route with the same polyline controls used by moving objects and configure the ant behavior in Properties.
Guide.Article.conveyors.Handles.Caption: Conveyor resize handles and an ant path.
Guide.Article.tubes.Title: Bamboo tubes and steam pipes
Guide.Article.tubes.Summary: Aim transport tubes and configure steam behavior.
Guide.Article.tubes.Bamboo: Rotate bamboo tubes to define their entrances and exits, then use Properties to pair or configure them as required by the object fields.
Guide.Article.tubes.Steam: Steam pipes use their orientation and properties to control the emitted force. Enable force fields to inspect the affected region while arranging nearby objects.
Guide.Article.tubes.Overlay.Caption: Bamboo and steam tubes with rotation and force overlays.
Guide.Article.rockets.Title: Rockets
Guide.Article.rockets.Summary: Aim rockets and tune launch behavior.
Guide.Article.rockets.Aim: Use the rotation dial to aim a rocket. Properties contains its gameplay values, including the launch impulse; use the inline field help when tuning unfamiliar values.
Guide.Article.rockets.Playtest.Tip: Preview the level in the game after changing impulse. The editor visualizes placement and direction but does not simulate full gameplay physics.
Guide.Article.rockets.Selected.Caption: A selected rocket with its direction and properties.
Guide.Article.mechanical-hands.Title: Mechanical hands
Guide.Article.mechanical-hands.Summary: Select, resize, split, and remove individual arm segments.
Guide.Article.mechanical-hands.Segments: A mechanical hand is edited segment by segment. Click a bone to select its segment, drag a joint to resize adjoining geometry, and drag the base to reposition the arm.
Guide.Article.mechanical-hands.Split: Hold Alt while hovering a bone to preview a new joint, then Alt-click to split the bone there. Right-click an existing joint to remove that segment.
Guide.Article.mechanical-hands.Dial.Note: The claw joint remains a resize target even when it overlaps the rotation dial, preventing an accidental segment rotation.
Mechanical-hand bones, joints, selected segment, and Alt split preview.
Guide.Article.tutorial-objects.Title: Tutorial icons and text
Guide.Article.tutorial-objects.Summary: Author instructional prompts and localized tutorial text.
Guide.Article.tutorial-objects.Text: Tutorial icons display familiar gesture prompts. Tutorial text supports authored text and wrapping; drag its width handle to change the wrap width while height follows the content.
Guide.Article.tutorial-objects.Editing: Select tutorial text and press F2 to edit it on the canvas. Enter accepts the edit; Shift-Enter inserts a line break.
Guide.Article.tutorial-objects.Language: Use the tutorial language picker to inspect one localized text variant at a time.
Guide.Article.tutorial-objects.Width.Cap: Tutorial icon and editable tutorial text width.
Guide.Article.object-reference.Title: Object reference
Guide.Article.object-reference.Summary: Understand the purpose of the standard palette objects.
Guide.Article.object-reference.Goals: Om Nom is the target, candy is the playable objective, and stars are optional collectibles. Split-candy levels use left and right candy halves.
Guide.Article.object-reference.Forces: Bubbles lift candy; air cushions push it; gravity buttons change gravity; bouncers redirect objects; spikes and electric sparks are hazards; and steam pipes apply force.
Guide.Article.object-reference.Mechanics: Light bulbs and lanterns support night mechanics. Ghosts change state, vinyl records spin, mice interact with cheese-themed behavior, and snails, rockets, tubes, conveyors, hats, ropes, hands, and paths provide more advanced movement.
Guide.Article.object-reference.Details.N: Select any palette object to see the exact fields supported by this editor. Complex object families have dedicated guide articles.
Guide.Article.menus-commands.Title: Menus and commands
Guide.Article.menus-commands.Summary: Find file, editing, viewing, and help commands.
Guide.Article.menus-commands.File: Create, open, save, playtest, choose the game location, export a screenshot, review changes, and close the current level.
Guide.Article.menus-commands.Edit: Undo and redo, clipboard and selection commands, grid and rotation snapping, and Level Settings.
Guide.Article.menus-commands.View: Zoom controls, animation preview, and diagnostic overlays for hitboxes, force fields, and movement paths.
Guide.Article.menus-commands.Help: Open this Usage Guide. About is also here on Windows, Linux, and the browser; macOS keeps About in the application menu.
Guide.Article.keyboard-shortcuts.Title: Keyboard shortcuts
Guide.Article.keyboard-shortcuts.Summary: Use the editor's global file, editing, preview, and zoom commands.
Guide.Article.keyboard-shortcuts.Platfor: Use Command instead of Ctrl on macOS. Redo is Command-Shift-Z on macOS and Ctrl-Y elsewhere.
Guide.Article.pointer-gestures.Title: Pointer, trackpad, and touch gestures
Guide.Article.pointer-gestures.Summary: Navigate and edit with a mouse, trackpad, touchscreen, or pen.
Guide.Article.pointer-gestures.Mouse: Drag empty canvas space or middle-drag to pan. Wheel scrolls vertically; Shift-wheel scrolls horizontally. Ctrl-wheel zooms around the pointer.
Guide.Article.pointer-gestures.Touch: Trackpad magnify and touchscreen pinch gestures zoom around their origin. Compact layouts also provide explicit Edit and Pan interaction modes for touch.
Guide.Article.pointer-gestures.Context: Right-click removes editable polyline points or mechanical-hand joints. Double-click an object to toggle its lock.
Guide.Article.modifier-keys.Title: Modifier keys
Guide.Article.modifier-keys.Summary: Learn when Command, Ctrl, Shift, and Alt change an editing gesture.
Guide.Article.modifier-keys.Shortcut.Sel: Add or remove an object from selection
Guide.Article.modifier-keys.Shortcut.Hor: Scroll horizontally with a vertical wheel
Guide.Article.modifier-keys.Option.Note: On macOS, the Alt key is labelled Option. The guide uses Alt when referring to Avalonia's cross-platform modifier.
Guide.Article.snapping.Title: Snapping and precision editing
Guide.Article.snapping.Toggles: Edit > Snap to grid controls positional snapping during placement and dragging. Edit > Snap rotation keeps supported rotation dials on their configured angular step.
Guide.Article.snapping.Temporary: Hold Alt during a rotation drag for temporary snapping without changing the persistent toggle. Hold Shift while editing a polyline to constrain the new segment angle.
Guide.Article.snapping.Properties.Tip: Use Properties after a visual edit when a coordinate, angle, length, or radius must be exact.
Guide.Article.animation-preview.Title: Animation preview
Guide.Article.animation-preview.Summary: Preview animated sprites for one object or the whole level.
Guide.Article.animation-preview.Usage: Choose View > Start animation preview or press Space to preview supported animations throughout the level. Use the play control on an object row to preview only that object.
Guide.Article.animation-preview.Scope.No: Animation preview shows visual animation, not complete game physics or object interactions.
Guide.Article.diagnostic-overlays.Title: Diagnostic overlays
Guide.Article.diagnostic-overlays.Summar: Inspect hitboxes, forces, and movement paths.
Guide.Article.diagnostic-overlays.Usage: The View menu can show hitboxes, force fields, and movement paths. These overlays help explain collision boundaries, active force regions, portal mouths, and off-selection movement routes.
Guide.Article.diagnostic-overlays.Editor: Overlays are editor-only diagnostics and are not written into the level as gameplay objects.
Guide.Article.diagnostic-overlays.Enable: A level with all three diagnostic overlays enabled.
Guide.Article.validation-review.Title: Validate and review changes
Guide.Article.validation-review.Summary: Catch likely gameplay problems and inspect the XML changes before saving.
Guide.Article.validation-review.Validati: Before save or playtest, validation reports likely problems such as missing candy or Om Nom, mismatched candy halves, invalid bindings, duplicate candy numbers, idle ghosts, and dangerous starting overlaps.
Guide.Article.validation-review.Review: File > Review Changes compares the live document with the last opened or saved version. Choose split or unified presentation and inspect additions, removals, and modifications.
Guide.Article.validation-review.Warnings: Warnings do not silently discard work. After reviewing them, you can return to editing or explicitly continue.
The validation prompt and Review Changes dialog.
Guide.Article.save-export-playtest.Title: Save, export, and playtest
Guide.Article.save-export-playtest.Summa: Save XML, export a rendered image, and launch the level in Cut the Rope: DX.
Guide.Article.save-export-playtest.Save: Save writes to the current file when the platform supports it; Save As chooses a new destination. Screenshot exports the rendered level as a PNG.
Guide.Article.save-export-playtest.Playt: Desktop builds can set the Cut the Rope: DX location and launch the current level with File > Playtest. The editor validates the level and writes a temporary playtest copy first.
Guide.Article.save-export-playtest.Brows: The browser cannot launch a local game executable. Download or save the level, then open it with your desktop workflow.
Guide.Article.troubleshooting.Title: Troubleshooting
Guide.Article.troubleshooting.Summary: Resolve missing assets, disabled objects, unexpected selection, and playtest problems.
Guide.Article.troubleshooting.SearchTerm: assets required|disabled palette|cannot select|playtest error|locked layer
Guide.Article.troubleshooting.Palette.He: An object is disabled in the palette
Guide.Article.troubleshooting.Palette: Check level mechanics in Level Settings. Some objects require half-candy or night-level configuration.
Guide.Article.troubleshooting.Selection: Check the object and its parent layer for hidden or locked state. If objects overlap, repeated clicks cycle through hits at the same location.
Guide.Article.troubleshooting.Playtest: Set the Cut the Rope: DX location again and confirm the selected application or executable still exists and is runnable.
Guide.Article.troubleshooting.Assets: Complete the guided asset setup by downloading supported assets or choosing a valid asset zip.

Attr.impulse.Help: Thrust strength determines how hard the rocket pushes the attached candy while firing. Higher values launch it faster and farther; 0 means no thrust.
Attr.impulseFactor.Help: Slack-rope thrust multiplier. While the rope tied to the rocket is loose, its thrust is scaled by this factor so the push eases off. Default 0.6; 1 keeps full thrust when slack, lower is gentler.
Hint.PolylinePointLimit: Movement path is at its 99-point limit

Validation.TwoPartHasPlainCandy: Two-part level shouldn't contain a plain candy.
Validation.NightNoBulb: Night level has no light bulb.
Validation.DuplicateSettingsLayer: Multiple settings layers found; only the first one is used.
Validation.DuplicateCandyNumber: Duplicate candyNumber values found; grabs cannot tell those candies apart.
Validation.GrabUnmatchedCandyNumber: A grab references candyNumber '{0}', which no candy has, it will bind to the primary candy.
Validation.GrabUnmatchedBulbNumber: A grab binds to bulbNumber '{0}', which no light bulb has.
Validation.GhostIdle: A ghost has no enabled states (grab/bubble/bouncer), it will sit idle and do nothing.
Validation.CandyInHazard: Candy {0} starts inside a spike and will break immediately.
Validation.CandyOnMouth: Candy {0} starts on Om Nom's mouth and will be eaten immediately, winning the level.
